title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description: Find the kth largest element in an array, using a size-capped min-heap instead of a full sort.

sections.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array

content.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array

blocks.text: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array. This means the kth largest element in sorted order, not the kth distinct value.

blocks.caption: A size-capped min-heap always holds the k largest numbers seen so far, with the smallest of them on top.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Field","Details"],"rows":[["Input","nums[] (may contain duplicates), k (1-indexed rank from the largest)"],["Output","The kth largest value (duplicates count individually, not as one distinct value)"]]}

blocks.text: "The kth largest (or smallest) element" is the classic signal for a size-capped heap: maintain a min-heap of size k, and whenever a new element would grow it beyond k, evict the smallest. Whatever remains at the top of the heap at the end is exactly the kth largest overall.

blocks.title: Connection
blocks.text: This exact size-capped-heap pattern reused across many problems in this project (Maximum Performance of a Team's speed heap, Maximum Number of Robots' deque) for maintaining "the k best candidates so far."

Picture a podium with only k spots, open to any new contender. Whenever a new contender is stronger than the weakest spot currently on the podium, that weakest spot is replaced. After every contender has been considered, the weakest spot remaining on the podium is exactly the kth strongest overall.

blocks.caption: The podium always holds the k strongest so far, with the weakest of them easily replaced.

items: Push every number into a min-heap.
Whenever the heap exceeds size k, pop the smallest, since it can no longer be among the top k.
After processing all numbers, the heap's top (the smallest of the remaining k) is exactly the kth largest.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Number processed","Heap after (size capped at 2)"],"rows":[["3","[3]"],["2","[2, 3]"],["1","[2, 3] (1 pushed then popped as the smallest)"],["5","[3, 5] (2 popped)"],["6","[5, 6] (3 popped)"],["4","[5, 6] (4 pushed then popped)"]]}

blocks.title: Answer
blocks.text: The final heap is [5, 6], with 5 on top (the smaller of the two), matching the expected output of 5, the 2nd largest value in the array.
The simplest approach sorts the entire array and reads off the kth-from-the-end element directly. This is correct and simple, but sorts the ENTIRE array even when k is small.

A size-capped min-heap only ever holds k elements at a time, doing less work overall when k is much smaller than n, since only the top k candidates are maintained rather than a full sorted order of everything.
Sort the entire array and read the kth-from-the-end element directly.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Metric","Value","Why"],"rows":[["Time","O(n log n)","Full sort of the entire array"],["Space","O(n)","The sorted copy"]]}

blocks.title: Bottleneck
blocks.text: Sorting the entire array does unnecessary work when only the top k elements actually matter, especially when k is much smaller than n.

Maintain a min-heap capped at size k. Push every number; whenever the heap exceeds k elements, pop the smallest. At the end, the heap's top is the kth largest element, since only the k largest values survive in the heap.

items: Push each number into the heap, O(log k) per push.
If the heap size exceeds k, pop the smallest, O(log k).
The heap top at the end is the answer, O(1) to read.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","Time","Space"],"rows":[["Brute Force, full sort","O(n log n)","O(n)"],["Optimized, size-capped min-heap","O(n log k)","O(k)"]]}

items: "The kth largest/smallest" is a strong signal for a size-capped heap, avoiding a full sort of the whole collection.
A min-heap capped at size k naturally surfaces the kth largest at its top, since anything weaker than the current top k is discarded immediately.
This pattern scales especially well when k is much smaller than the total input size n.

blocks.text: Kth Largest Element in an Array is solved with a min-heap capped at size k: every number is pushed, and the smallest is evicted whenever the heap exceeds k elements. The heap's top at the end is exactly the kth largest, giving O(n log k) time instead of a full O(n log n) sort.
